name: tie
description: ThisIsEnough — lightweight file-first workflow that keeps the user's mental model, the agent's understanding, and the codebase in sync. A user-approved checklist gates implementation, a committed ARCHITECTURE.md (constitution + map) replaces per-session codebase re-scanning, and each run is five files driven through plan, implement, verify, and fix loops.

interface.shortDescription: Sync on a requirement, approve its checklist, then let the orchestrator drive plan → implement → verify → fix until done or blocked.
interface.longDescription: ThisIsEnough is a lightweight file-first workflow runtime. tie:requirements syncs the user's mental model with the agent's understanding and the codebase, capturing agreements and a core checklist in a draft spec under .tie/drafts/. Implementation starts only after the user approves that checklist. The orchestrator then runs the approved draft (or an ad-hoc requirement, still gated by one confirmation) through Planner (technical direction), Implementer (implementation), and Verifier (checklist verification plus adjacent-flow checks), looping fixes within limits. Each run is exactly five files under .tie/runs/<run-id>/, with .tie/active_run pointing at the current run and the whole .tie/ directory gitignored. Durable knowledge lives in a committed ARCHITECTURE.md (constitution + map), updated incrementally during runs; tie:map creates or resyncs it outside a run. tie:resume continues an interrupted run and tie:doctor diagnoses and safely repairs workflow state.
defaultPrompt: Sync on this requirement and draft the spec with tie:requirements:
Start a run from my approved draft:
Create or resync ARCHITECTURE.md with tie:map.
Diagnose this workflow state with tie:doctor.
